title: Hero Variant Lab — Q2 launch copy experiments
content:
Purpose:
This working doc collects hero and tagline variants for the public homepage and product landing routes ahead of the Q2 marketing push. Aim: quick iterations that map to measurable funnels (signup, api key creation, demo requests). We prioritize clarity on 1) what we deliver, 2) who it is for, 3) why it beats simple managed endpoints and self-hosting.

Audience buckets (prioritized):
- Small to mid-size product teams (PLG motion): want fast time-to-value + predictable cost
- Platform/infra teams at enterprise: need predictable latency, private deployments, and SLAs
- ML engineers: care about quantization, batching, and runtime control

Tone & constraints:
- Concise hero copy, single-line headline + 1-sentence subhead + 1-line CTA
- Avoid technical jargon in hero; surface developer-first stance and production economics
- Provide explicit differentiator snippets in subcopy for engineers and infra buyers

Hero options (A/B candidates) — short, test-ready variants:
Variant A (velocity + economics):
Headline: Ship LLM features faster, run them cheaper
Subhead: One API for hosted, reserved, and private inference—predictable latency and lower token costs out of the box
Primary CTA: Try the Hosted API — free credits
Secondary CTA: Compare Dedicated plans
Why this works: Balances time-to-value and cost, appeals to builders and growth teams.

Variant B (reliability + control):
Headline: Production-grade LLM inference, without the infrastructure headache
Subhead: High-throughput runtime, smart routing and fallbacks, and enterprise controls for private deployments
Primary CTA: See SLAs & pricing
Secondary CTA: Request private deployment info
Why: Strong for enterprise pages and hero for Dedicated customers.

Variant C (developer-first technical):
Headline: Deterministic latency. Transparent token economics. One runtime to serve them all.
Subhead: GPU-optimized kernels, KV caching, and model routing that keep SLAs intact under load
Primary CTA: Start a technical demo
Secondary CTA: Read the architecture brief
Why: Targets ML/infra engineers; emphasizes predictable behavior and observable metrics.

Microcopy / CTA variants to A/B test:
- Try Redwood — free credits
- Start a 5-minute API key
- Launch a dedicated trial
- Request a private deployment consult

Supporting subblocks for product landing pages (short bullets, 3 items max):
- Unified API: hosted, dedicated, and private with the same developer experience
- Cost controls: batching, prefix caching, and quantization suggestions to reduce unit cost
- Reliability: multi-region routing, automatic fallbacks, and SLA-backed plans

Positioning framings for subhead / above-the-fold panels (engineer, infra, exec):
- Engineer: "Ship once, run anywhere — same SDK, lower latency surprises."
- Infra lead: "Predictable throughput with reserved capacity and burst options."
- Exec/PO: "Lower TCO for LLM features while preserving control and compliance."

Competitive differentiators to call out (short lines to place near hero or in comparison block):
- Unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, private: avoid vendor lock and rewrite cycles
- Observable unit economics: token-level cost breakdowns and routing cost controls
- Graceful degradation: automatic fallback to lower-cost/compatible variants during contention

Rapid objection handling lines (for FAQ / near-hero tooltips):
Q: How is this different from managed endpoints?
A: We provide a high-throughput runtime plus orchestration and cost controls; managed endpoints focus on access, we focus on production economics and predictable latency.
Q: Can I run on my VPC?
A: Yes — Private deployments with customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM options.

Experiment plan (minimum viable A/B test):
- Test variants A vs B on homepage for 2 weeks, targeting traffic from product hunt + organic blog posts
- Primary metric: new API keys created per 1k visitors
- Secondary metrics: demo requests, bounce rate at 10s
- Traffic split: 50/50; early stop rules for statistically significant delta at p<0.05 for primary metric

Measurement & instrumentation checklist:
- Event: homepage_variant_shown (variant id)
- Event: api_key_created (source, variant id)
- Funnel: hero_click -> start_signup -> api_key_created
- Add UTM tags for campaign sources (ph, twitter, newsletter)

Launch timeline (Q2 sprint cadence):
- Week 1: Lock A/B variants and build hero blocks in staging
- Week 2: Instrument analytics and QA on mobile/desktop
- Week 3-4: Run test, monitor, collect results
- Week 5: Choose winner and roll to global pages

Risks / open questions:
- Need to validate that messaging about "lower token costs" is defensible without complex footnotes — coordinate with product pricing to avoid overpromising
- How much technical detail to surface on the homepage vs product landing? Recommend: keep hero high-level, surface technical callouts farther down with an anchor link to architecture brief
- Localization: English-first; schedule translations after variant learns

Next steps (owners):
- Priya: finalize 3 hero creatives and hand off to design (due 2026-03-05)
- Ethan: implement analytics events and A/B framework (due 2026-03-10)
- Marisol: coordinate copy review with product and legal (due 2026-03-03)

Appendix: 6 extra short taglines to stash for social and ad copy:
- "Serve LLMs with confidence."
- "Inference that scales — predictably."
- "From prototype to production, painlessly."
- "Control the cost, keep the quality."
- "Your runtime for real-world LLMs."
- "Make latency predictable, not accidental."

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally compact; prefer simple quantitative tests over long qualitative debates. Please comment with preferred hero variant and any fatal copy/legal concerns by 2026-02-28.
